findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:408-424 buffers the jobs SSE with response.text() before parseRunnerJobsAvailableSse runs, so a normal long-lived text/event-stream body will not surface an early jobs.available event to the runner; it will wait until the body closes or the timeout aborts, then packages/main/src/core/authority-runner.ts:438-456 falls back to claim only after that wait. This keeps the signed claim authority boundary safe, but it means the CLI does not actually consume a persistent /v1/runners/{runnerId}/jobs/stream notification hint promptly; the smoke test only covers a bounded SSE-looking response that closes after the event, not a real long-lived stream.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 86a50393d: streamRunnerJobsAvailable now uses bounded body reader and returns on the first classifiable jobs.available event from a long-lived text/event-stream instead of waiting for response.text() close/timeout. Verified by smoke long-lived stream scenario and build.

findings.desc: authority-runner-client-smoke exercises a positive jobs.available SSE hint followed by a signed claim, but the fake claim response is {"job":null} and the smoke never asserts out.claimedJobId stays null or that ownership/authority is derived only from the claim response. A regression could populate claimedJobId from SSE jobIds while still preserving the tested GET-before-POST order and claim_job ok event, so CHK-001 adversarial no-overclaim coverage is incomplete. Add an assertion/scenario that positive SSE + null or failed claim does not produce claimedJobId/releasedJobId/authority completion, and only a JobSpec returned by the signed claim can create ownership.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 86a50393d: smoke asserts positive SSE jobIds plus signed claim {job:null} leaves claimedJobId and releasedJobId null, proving SSE is not ownership. Verified by authority-runner-client-smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:413-424 awaits response.text() before parsing SSE. With a real long-lived text/event-stream response that writes event: jobs.available/data {"count":1,"jobIds":["job-1"]} and keeps the connection open, streamRunnerJobsAvailable returns kind=timeout/status=200 instead of available, so runLatticeAuthorityControlPlaneOnce waits for the timeout before signed claim rather than immediately attempting claim as CHK-001 requires. Repro command used in review: npm --prefix packages/main run build -- --pretty false, then a local node --input-type=module HTTP SSE probe returned {"kind":"timeout","ok":false,"status":200} after the event was sent.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 86a50393d: real body-stream SSE is parsed incrementally and returns available promptly; fallback remains for text-only stubs and malformed/timeout cases. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build and node packages/main/dist/tasks/authority-runner-client-smoke.js.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:2845-2867 still stops reading a real long-lived SSE stream after a complete non-jobs.available block when prefix.remainder is empty. A normal stream can send a heartbeat/comment block first and jobs.available later; an inline Node probe against packages/main/dist/core/authority-client.js returned kind=unavailable status=200 with the first-event-block fallback in 1ms for chunks [: heartbeat, then jobs.available 25ms later]. That means 86a50393d only returns promptly when heartbeat and jobs.available are already buffered together, not when jobs.available is the first later classifiable event. The signed-claim ownership boundary remains intact, but the F-001/F-003 incremental long-lived stream fix is incomplete.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f2a04329e: stream reader now ignores heartbeat/comment/non-jobs blocks and continues reading even when remainder is empty, with reads tied to abort signal. Smoke covers standalone heartbeat chunk followed by later jobs.available on non-closing stream.

findings.desc: Round 2 test-coverage gap: the new long-lived stream smoke covers a non-closing body stream only when the first chunk already contains both a complete heartbeat block and the following event: jobs.available line. A normal long-lived SSE stream can flush a standalone heartbeat/comment block first and emit jobs.available later; current readRunnerJobsAvailableSseStream returns unavailable at packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:2845-2867 when prefix.remainder is empty after that first block, and the smoke at packages/main/src/tasks/authority-runner-client-smoke.ts:316-339 would not catch it. F-002 no-overclaim is covered by the claimedJobId/releasedJobId null assertions, but stream parsing coverage is still incomplete for heartbeat-first long-lived streams.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f2a04329e: added smoke coverage for heartbeat-first long-lived SSE where jobs.available arrives in a later chunk; node smoke proves jobs_stream ok and signed claim still happens.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:2845-2867 returns unavailable as soon as the first complete SSE block lacks jobs.available and prefix.remainder is empty. With a normal native-fetch text/event-stream that writes a standalone heartbeat/comment block (`: heartbeat\n\n`) and then writes `event: jobs.available` 50ms later, streamRunnerJobsAvailable returns kind=unavailable in ~18ms before the job event is read, so the runner misses the push hint and falls back to signed claim/polling early. Repro used in review: node --input-type=module local HTTP SSE probe against AuthorityClient with 1000ms timeout; observed {kind:"unavailable", status:200, message:"first event block did not contain jobs.available"}. The existing smoke keeps heartbeat and partial jobs.available in the same chunk, so it does not cover heartbeat and jobs.available delivered as separate SSE writes.
